results.title: Fifa World Cup: All Whites selection race heats up as coach Darren Bazeley weighs starting XI for Iran - NZ Herald
highlights:
Fifa World Cup: All
[...]
selection race heats up as coach Darren Bazeley weighs starting XI for Iran - NZ Herald
[...]
All Whites coach Darren Bazeley is adamant that success at this tournament will take a full squad effort.
[...]
While most of the starting XI for the Iran game next Monday (Tuesday NZT) seem to be locked in, there are still three – or maybe four – spots up for grabs.
[...]
But beyond those who are on the field for kickoff, reinforcements will be vital, both in the second half of the match and in the next two group games. That’s partly because the bench impact picture has changed so dramatically over the years.
[...]
Bazeley’s palette is much wider. He is permitted five substitutes each game and will be allowed a sixth, should the All Whites make the knockout stages and end up in an extra-time scenario.
[...]
It means he is able to make the most of the squad’s depth, particularly on both flanks, and it is a healthy problem to have for the selection panel of Bazeley and his assistants Simon Elliott, Tony Readings and Paul Gothard.
[...]
“We talk every day
[...]
the squad around the potentials, and we possibly have two or three different teams in our heads,” Bazeley said today.
[...]
“Eighty per cent of them are the same [but] we will have quite a few people play at this World Cup, with good options off the bench.”
[...]
As the Herald revealed yesterday, Bazeley is aiming to name his starting team before training on June 12 (San Diego time), giving three full days to work with those selected in formation.
[...]
But he said that there are still “good options and choices” and plenty to weigh up before the final call is made.
[...]
“There are good choices in every position now but some are a little bit tighter than others,” Bazeley said.
[...]
Tuesday’s session (San Diego time) was a landmark one, with all 26 players taking part in the full session, since the squad assembled two weeks ago. Ryan Thomas has recovered from the hamstring issue – though realistically is a bench option for Iran – while Joe Bell (calf) and Callan Elliot (head knock) also got through.
[...]
From tomorrow, the team will enter the official Fifa bubble, training at the University of San Diego. It’s the culmination of a long preparation phase, which started in Miami with just four players, then five, nine and 10 before the whole group arrived in the last week of May.

results.title: All Whites star Ryan Thomas on track for Fifa World Cup opener, despite injury scare - NZ Herald
highlights:
# All Whites star Ryan Thomas on track for Fifa World Cup opener, despite injury scare - NZ Herald
[...]
All Whites star Ryan Thomas is confident he will be ready for the World Cup opener against Iran – despite an untimely hamstring injury picked up on club duty last month.
[...]
Thomas is one of the most important players in the New Zealand squad, a fixture in that next cohort of four or five just below skipper Chris Wood. That’s because of his experience, his leadership and, most of all, his ability on the ball – he’s able to navigate tight areas and find space like few others in the All Whites, especially in the final third. But his buildup to this tournament has been compromised, after a hamstring strain suffered while playing for his Dutch club PEC Zwolle.
[...]
In that match – against Heracles Almelo – Thomas set up the decisive goal in the 1-0 win before he got what he described as a “little tear” in his hamstring. Though he would have feared the worst at the time it has responded well to treatment and rest and he has done some light training away from the group since he came into camp in the United States last Wednesday.
[...]
The 31-year-old took no part in training on Thursday (Friday NZT), but will rejoin the group for the light pre-game session on Friday, though he won’t be in contention for any minutes against England on Saturday (Sunday NZT). Missing both warm-up matches is far from ideal but Thomas is still likely to be used against Iran – if his fitness continues to track in the right direction – even if it is off the bench.
[...]
Fellow midfielder Joe Bell is also on track, after missing the 4-0 loss to Haiti on Wednesday (NZT) for a similar reason. The 27-year-old picked up a calf injury playing for Norwegian club Viking FK in early May, which saw him miss their last three matches. He joined the All Whites last week and has been slowly building back into full training mode.
[...]
“It’s been a little bit of timeout for me, which is unusual but I have been building in really
[...]
... the physio has been fantastic,” Bell said. “I’ve been taking it a bit cautious, making sure the body’s in the right place going into these huge [World Cup] games … but on track so looking good.”
[...]
Bell took a full part in Thursday’s session (Friday NZT) and expected to see some game time against England, as the team look to reset quickly after the chastening 4-0 defeat to Haiti in Fort Lauderdale on Wednesday.
[...]
Fullback Callan Elliott is the other player in doubt, after taking a shot in the face against Haiti. Though the medical staff have ruled out concussion, he is being monitored for any symptoms and sat out training on Thursday.

results.title: New Zealand begin final countdown to FIFA World Cup 2026™ | Oceania Football Confederation

[...]

highlights:
Football: All Whites midfielders Ryan and Bell to miss World Cup warm-ups with injuries | RNZ News
[...]
New Zealand midfielders Ryan Thomas and Joe Bell will head into the World Cup short of match practice while nursing leg injuries.
[...]
Coach Darren Bazeley told Stuff that Thomas will miss friendlies against Haiti on Tuesday and England on Saturday while recovering from a hamstring strain.
[...]
Bell will miss at least the Haiti match due to a calf issue.
[...]
Bazeley is hopeful both will be available for their World Cup opener against Iran on 15 June but their absence is a setback for the staff's midfield planning.
[...]
With the duo sidelined, Alex Rufer and rookie midfielder Lachlan Bayliss will likely start in the midfield with regular Marko Stamenic against Haiti in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.
